title: 1952 AHSME Problem 36
statement: To be continuous at \(x=-1,\) the value of \(\dfrac{x^3+1}{x^2-1}\) is taken to be:

solutions.text:
For \(x\ne-1,\) \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{x^3+1}{x^2-1} &=\frac{(x+1)(x^2-x+1)} {(x+1)(x-1)}\\ &=\frac{x^2-x+1}{x-1}. \end{aligned} \] Its limit at \(x=-1\) is \[ \frac{1+1+1}{-2}=-\frac32. \] Assigning this value removes the discontinuity.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Factor both numerator and denominator before substituting \(x=-1\)
Cancel the common factor \(x+1\) and evaluate the remaining expression
